title: Senior's toolkit: containers in production
summary: Read exits, health, memory and disk; run containers with limits and least privilege; keep secrets out of images.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: containers in production
steps.body: On call, a container has crashed, is unhealthy, or the host disk is full. These commands tell you which, and the run flags keep it from happening again.

toolkit.what: Why it died: the exit code, and whether the kernel killed it for using too much memory.
flags: SIGKILL: usually OOM (check `OOMKilled`) or a `docker kill`
the app threw and exited; read the logs

toolkit.what: The healthcheck status and the output of its last runs, so you see exactly why it says unhealthy.
flags: the last checks with exit code and output

toolkit.what: CPU, memory against its limit, network and disk IO for every container, once.
flags: one snapshot instead of a live screen

toolkit.what: Docker's own timeline: which containers died, were OOM-killed or restarted, and when.
Disk used by images, containers, volumes and the build cache, and how much of it can be reclaimed.
flags: drop build cache older than 3 days
drop unused images older than a week
toolkit.example: docker system df && docker builder prune -f --filter until=72h
toolkit.when: "no space left on device" on a host or CI runner

toolkit.what: Runs with limits and least privilege, the way production should: bounded memory and CPU, an immutable filesystem, no Linux capabilities.
flags: hard memory limit and CPU share
a tiny PID 1 that forwards signals and reaps zombies
toolkit.example: docker run -d --name api --memory 512m --cpus 1 --read-only --tmpfs /tmp --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --init --restart unless-stopped myorg/api:1.4.0

toolkit.what: Gives one build step a secret (a registry token, a .npmrc) without it ever reaching a layer or the image history.

steps.prompt: `api` restarts every few minutes. `docker ps -a` shows `Exited (137)`, and the logs end mid-request with no exception. What do you run first?
options: `docker inspect -f '{{.State.OOMKilled}}' api` and `docker stats --no-stream` to compare memory with the limit
`docker logs --tail 1000 api` to look for the exception
steps.explain: 137 is SIGKILL, and no exception means the process was killed from outside. `OOMKilled: true` confirms the memory limit; then fix a leak or raise `--memory`. The app never gets to log an OOM kill.

steps.prompt: Match each exit code to its usual meaning.
pairs: the app failed and exited; read its logs
killed with SIGKILL, often out of memory

steps.prompt: The CI runner fails every job with `no space left on device` during `docker build`. What do you run?
options: `docker system df`, then `docker builder prune` and `docker image prune -a` with an age filter
steps.explain: `system df` shows whether the build cache or old images fill the disk (it is usually the build cache). Prune with an `until` filter so today's cache stays. Deleting `/var/lib/docker` under a running daemon corrupts it.

steps.prompt: Run `api` with a 512 MB limit, no capabilities, a read-only root filesystem and a proper PID 1.
steps.explain: `--memory` sets the hard limit, `--cap-drop ALL` removes every capability, `--read-only` freezes the image filesystem (`--tmpfs /tmp` gives scratch space), `--init` forwards signals so `docker stop` is quick.

steps.prompt: Which flag belongs in a production `docker run`, and which is a red flag?
items: `-e DB_PASSWORD=...` typed in a shared shell script

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: For any crash, read the exit code and `OOMKilled` before the logs: they tell you whether the app failed or was killed. Give every production container a memory limit, `--cap-drop ALL` and `--init`, and put `docker system df` in your runner maintenance.
